newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African shares recovered early losses and ended Tuesday in positive territory as golds launched a mini-rally to claw back some of Monday's steep fall, dealers said.
The overall rise was partly inspired by bullion's successful efforts to climb back over the $320 an ounce level and so provide some desperately needed short-term support to the ailing golds index.
But dealers warned gold shares were not out of trouble yet.

"People have been trying to call the bottom for bullion and they might have got this rally right, but there is still some downside to come," said James Scott, equity marketing manager at Societe Generale Frankel Pollak.
Golds put on 19.8 points, or 2.19 percent, to 923.7 and so recovered about half their Monday losses.
In the wider market encouraging buying from overseas overcame early negative local sentiment and the afternoon saw brisk business after a lacklustre start to the week.
Overall there were 172 shares that headed down, against 184 that posted gains.

About 928 million rands worth of trade changed hands with trade boosted by overseas buying in Coronation "N" shares that saw the stock add 275 cents to 85.50 rand in trade worth 77.65 million rand. Coronation Holdings rose 300 cents to 95.50 rand.
Trade was also boosted by one broker's sale offshore of a basket of blue-chip shares, dealers said.
The all-share index ended up 17.1 points to 7,310.3 as the industrials index added 23.3 points to 8,766.3.
Dealers said the market would probably try and hold the gains on Wednesday after seeing two successive days of heavy selling that had left some stocks looking a touch oversold.
"It shoud try and stick around here," one dealer said.
Amongst individual shares to catch the market's eye was a flood of rumours that ignited music to retailing group CNA-Gallo Ltd with speculation that stores firm Pick'n Pay Ltd is in talks to buy it.
CNA-Gallo ended up 54 cents, or 13.99 percent, to 440 cents. Pick'n Pay shares were up 20 cents to match their year high of 720 cents.
Another gainer was media group Sasani Ltd which rallied from some recent heavy losses that have stripped more than 30 percent off the stock's value in the past three weeks.
Sasani finished up nine cents to 96 cents.

Shares in iron and steel producer Iscor Ltd fell to a new 1997 low following reports that it was considering mothballing its Pretoria steel mill, so endangering 1,400 jobs, but later recovered lost ground to end unchanged at 287 cents.
Among falling shares Lenco Holdings Ltd toppled on news that talks with Malbak Ltd had been called off. Lenco dropped 95 cents to 540 cents, while Malbak was unchanged at 690 cents.
In the futures market dealers said there had been some tentative buying into the spot market.
Contracts followed equities up and recovered most of their losses after a shakey early start.
The September all-share contract was last at 6,657/65 from 6,669 as the industrials contract was at 8,495/508 from 8,509. The golds contract was at 642/55 from 634.
-- Paul Harris, Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482 1003
